findings.desc: CHK-001:edge:1 lacks a concrete bound check: the intent requires writeProposal to be tested with a path-traversal id (e.g. ../etc/passwd) to confirm it is sanitized or rejected without writing outside proposals/. The safeProposalId guard exists in learning-store.ts but the smoke contains no check that invokes writeProposal (or the handler) with such an id and asserts the expected rejection. The evidence note is a generic-fallback description that covers all 9 CHK-001 intents identically; it does not state that this specific adversarial boundary was exercised.

findings.desc: CHK-001:adversarial:1 has no verificationEvidence binding to any concurrent-write test: the intent requires writeProposal called concurrently with the same id to produce last-write-wins or an atomic error, never corrupted JSON. The smoke contains zero concurrency checks and the evidence record reuses the identical generic note and command as the happy-path entries (all 9 CHK-001 evidence records share the same note: 'playbook+proposal types; learning-store round-trips playbooks.json+proposals/...'). There is no waiver explaining why this must-intent is exempted from automation. This is an uncovered must-intent.

findings.desc: handlers/playbook.ts:46-52 nextProposalId reads only proposals/ directory (listProposals) and does NOT consult playbooks.json; after a full lifecycle round (propose->approve->proposal deleted), the proposals/ dir is empty and the counter resets to PBP-001; a second propose then mints another PBP-001, and approving it produces two entries with identical id in playbooks.json. Reproducible with: propose F-001 (PBP-001), approve, then propose F-002 -> also PBP-001, approve -> readPlaybooks() returns [{id:'PBP-001',...},{id:'PBP-001',...}]. Fix: read both proposals/ and existing playbooks.json in nextProposalId to derive the global max; or assign IDs from playbooks.json length+1.
